query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of grain boundary segregation or nano-precipitates in Equal-atomic NbMoTaW can improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance.

generation.intervention: Introduction of grain boundary segregation or nano-precipitates through controlled processing conditions

generation.mechanism: Grain boundary segregation or nano-precipitates reduce grain boundary energy and promote dislocation mobility, enhancing room-temperature ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in room-temperature ductility, maintained mechanical performance at 1600 °C, and maintained irradiation resistance

generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of grain boundary segregation or nano-precipitates required to achieve improved room-temperature ductility is uncertain
